Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

predictmeans 1.1.1.9000 (development version)

Changes that affect results or scripts

  • Permutation tests of mixed models decorrelate residuals with the symmetric square root of their covariance instead of the Cholesky factor: permmodels() for lme, gls and lmer models and permlmer() (so permanova.lmer()). The Cholesky factor depends on the order of the data (it treats the first unit of each block differently), so results changed when the data were sorted differently, and tests of terms that vary within blocks rejected too often: in simulations 6-8% of true null hypotheses at the 5% level, increasing with the number of blocks; 5.2-5.3% with the symmetric root (dev/permutation-plan.md, §3.3). Permutation p-values of these functions therefore differ from earlier versions. The root is computed from q x q matrices (q random effects), without forming any n x n matrix, so it is also much faster with crossed random effects: 0.11 s instead of 3.9 s for n = 3000, and 21 s for n = 20000, where the Cholesky factor took over 30 minutes and 2.9 GB. Confirmed with the package functions (1000 data sets each): permlmer() split plot 5.9%, crossed design 5.4% (6.4% before); permmodels() with no fixed effects 4.8% (lmer, 6.2-7.1% before) and 5.9% (lme).

  • Kenward-Roger adjusted standard errors are now the default for lmer models fitted by REML, in predictmeans() and contrastmeans() (vcov_adjust = TRUE). This matches SAS DDFM=KR and emmeans. Standard errors, confidence limits, SEDs, LSDs and p-values can differ slightly from predictmeans 1.x (e.g. 7.896 instead of 7.887 for an unbalanced Oats example); balanced designs barely change. Use vcov_adjust = FALSE to reproduce 1.x results.

  • glmmTMB is no longer attached by library(predictmeans); it moved from Depends to Imports. Scripts that fit models with glmmTMB() need library(glmmTMB). lme4, nlme and lmerTest are still attached.

  • permmodels() gives the same tables (including Satterthwaite df and p-values) whether an lmer model was fitted with lme4::lmer() or lmerTest::lmer().

  • glmer Poisson models now give back-transformed means as counts (whole numbers, never below zero), as glm and glmmTMB Poisson models already did.

  • semipred() limits are now two-sided at the stated level: the default level = 0.05 gives 95% limits. Earlier versions used qnorm(1 - level), i.e. 90% limits with the default; level = 0.1 gives those limits.

  • predictmeans(letterCI = TRUE) now works with atvar: the CI-overlap letters compare the means within each atvar group (as in predictmeans 1.1.2). Before, atvar was dropped and the letters compared all means. The note under the mean table now says the letters come from the overlap of, e.g., 83.4% CIs, and gives the approximate test level (about 0.05), instead of “significant level ‘0.166’”. level keeps its meaning (it sets the CIs). With two atvar factors the note is one line (“at each level of A:B”) instead of two.

Stable result tables

  • predictmeans() results gain three slots with fixed names and unrounded values. tidy() (generics/broom) and as.data.frame() return them:
    • means: one row per mean, with estimate, std.error, df, conf.low, conf.high, back-transformed response columns, group letters, n and estimable;
    • pairs: one row per comparison, with level1, level2, by (for atvar), estimate, std.error, df, statistic, p.value, p.adj, lsd and p.method;
    • settings. They are checked against emmeans in the tests. The legacy slots and the printed output are unchanged, and the result has class c("predictmeans", "pdmlist").
  • coef() and vcov() on a predictmeans() result give the means (model scale) and their covariance matrix, Kenward-Roger adjusted when the means are (equal to emmeans’ vcov()). Any contrast of the means can then be tested with multcomp::glht() or marginaleffects::hypotheses(), e.g. hypotheses(pm, hypothesis = "pairwise") (marginaleffects is in Suggests; predictmeans registers its get_coef/set_coef/get_vcov methods; recent marginaleffects versions also need options(marginaleffects_model_classes = "predictmeans")).

Plots and summaries from the result tables

  • autoplot() for predictmeans() results gives ggplot objects that work in Shiny, reports and plotly::ggplotly():
    • type = "means", with confidence limits, half-LSD bars or no bars;
    • type = "pvalue", a heatmap of the adjusted pairwise p-values in the colour bands of PMplot(), one panel per atvar level;
    • type = "response", the back-transformed means.
  • summary() prints the means with a footer stating the model and df method, the SED and LSD ranges, the p-value method and adjustment, what the letters mean, and the covariate values used.
  • Both read only the means and pairs tables: they compute nothing new, open no graphics device and print nothing unless printed.

Supporting new model classes

  • Kmatrix(), predictmeans(), contrastmeans() and covariatemeans() now get what they need from a model through six exported generics:
    • pm_coef(), pm_vcov(): estimates and their covariance;
    • pm_basis(): design matrix for new data;
    • pm_data(): the fitting data;
    • pm_df(): df for each contrast;
    • pm_linkinv(): inverse link.
    The defaults work for any class with the usual coef, vcov, terms, df.residual and family methods. Supporting another class means writing methods for these generics only (see ?pm_coef), and model classes predictmeans doesn’t know are no longer rejected. Built-in classes behave exactly as before.
  • Ordered factors keep their contrasts in the reference grid even when a model class stores no contrasts.

Named contrasts

  • New specify_contrast() writes contrasts with level names instead of counted columns, e.g. specify_contrast(Kmatrix(fm, "A:B"), a = (x:b1+y:b1)/2 -z:b1). The result goes straight into contrastmeans(ctrmatrix = ). It checks that the weights sum to zero (unless .zero_sum = FALSE) and that no missing or non-estimable mean is used.
  • contrastmeans():
    • accepts a contrast matrix whose columns are named by level, in any order and for a subset of levels;
    • keeps the contrast names in its result;
    • gains weights.

New options

  • permmodels(method = "freedman-lane") for lm and aov models: each term (and coefficient) is tested by permuting the residuals of the model without it and adding them back to that model’s fitted values (Freedman and Lane 1983). Use it when a covariate with extreme values is related to the tested term: in a simulation study (dev/sim-freedman-lane.md) permuting the response then rejected 6-7% of true null hypotheses at the 5% level, Freedman-Lane 4-5%; in other designs the two agreed. The statistics come from QR projections of blocks of permuted responses, with no refits (4999 permutations of a 1000-row model with 16 tests take about 11 seconds on one core). Weights and offsets are allowed; permlist is NULL, so the result cannot be passed to predictmeans(). The default, method = "raw", is unchanged. For mixed models with such a covariate the help page recommends the Kenward-Roger or Satterthwaite F test: the raw scheme was slightly liberal there (6.3%), the F test kept 5%.

  • New bootmodels(): parametric bootstrap p-values for the terms and coefficients of lmer and glmer models, simulating from the model without its fixed effects (global null) and refitting. Its result can be passed to predictmeans() and contrastmeans() as permlist, giving bootstrap p-values for pairwise comparisons and contrasts (p.method "bootstrap" in the pairs table).

  • semipred(simultaneous = TRUE) gives simultaneous confidence bands over the whole curve(s), and over difference curves with contr (Ruppert, Wand and Carroll): the critical value is the quantile of the largest standardised deviation from 10,000 draws, with a fixed seed so results repeat (the user’s random numbers are left alone).

  • predictmeans() accepts semireg() fits: the means of a factor term include the smooth terms (fixed part plus the smooth’s random effects, as semipred()), at the covariates’ means or at named covariate values, with pairwise comparisons (normal-based, any adj), letters, and coef()/vcov(). The result holds the means, pairs and settings tables. semipred()’s design step is now an internal function shared by both (its output is unchanged).

  • New R2_model(): R-squared of a mixed model as numbers (class "pm_r2", printed as percentages). method = "piepho" (default) gives the values of R2_glmm() as proportions; method = "nakagawa" gives Nakagawa and Schielzeth’s marginal and conditional R-squared, with random slopes as Johnson (2014), for gaussian and binomial models (sleepstudy: 0.279 and 0.799, as performance::r2_nakagawa()). R2_glmm() is unchanged.

  • New pm_slopes(): the slope of a numeric covariate within each level of a factor term, with SEs, df, confidence limits and tests, and pairwise comparisons of the slopes (any adj). Equal to emmeans’ emtrends() (Kenward-Roger for lmer); for poly() or splines the slope is taken at at (default: the covariate’s mean) by a central difference.

  • Response scale: when the means are back-transformed (non-identity link or trans), the means table has response.std.error (delta method, equal to emmeans with type = "response"). For a log link or trans = exp, the pairs table has the ratio of the means with its confidence limits (ratio, ratio.conf.low, ratio.conf.high); for a logit link, the odds ratio (odds.ratio, …). The limits use the same df as the differences.

  • New pm_joint(): F tests of sets of contrasts among the means of a term. With by, the means are compared within each level of the by factor(s), as SAS SLICE (e.g. nitrogen within each variety); with ctrmatrix, any set of contrasts is tested together. For lmer: the Kenward-Roger F test equal to pbkrtest::KRmodcomp(), or Satterthwaite equal to lmerTest::contest(joint = TRUE), or containment df; nlme df for lme; residual df otherwise.

  • New contrast_family() builds the standard families of contrasts among the means of a term for contrastmeans(): "pairwise", "revpairwise", "trt.vs.ctrl" (Dunnett; exact with adj = "mvt"), "consec", "poly" (integer orthogonal polynomials), "eff" and "del.eff", optionally within each level of by factors. Coefficients and names are emmeans’; results through contrastmeans() equal emmeans’ contrast().

  • New adj methods in predictmeans() and contrastmeans(): "sidak", "scheffe" and "mvt", as in emmeans (equal to emmeans’ p-values for sidak and scheffe; within 1e-3 for mvt). "mvt" is the single-step multivariate t adjustment, the exact counterpart of SAS ADJUST=SIMULATE; it needs mvtnorm (Suggests), uses a fixed seed so results repeat, and leaves the user’s random numbers as they were. The Scheffe rank is the number of means - 1 for pairs (within each atvar group) and the rank of ctrmatrix in contrastmeans(). With permlist only "sidak" of the three is allowed.

  • Kmatrix(), predictmeans() and covariatemeans() gain weights = c("equal", "proportional", "outer", "cells", "flat"), which sets how the cells of the factors not in modelterm are weighted. "proportional" uses the observed frequencies, the same for every mean, like SAS LSMEANS / OM. The definitions are emmeans’, and the results match emmeans. The default "equal" is unchanged.

  • predictmeans(vcov_adjust = TRUE) and contrastmeans(vcov_adjust = TRUE): for lmer models fitted by REML, standard errors use the Kenward-Roger adjusted covariance (as SAS DDFM=KR and emmeans do) to go with the Kenward-Roger df. The default keeps the earlier, unadjusted standard errors.

  • predictmeans() and covariatemeans() pass cov_reduce and exclude on to Kmatrix(). For example, cov_reduce = "average" gives gam means adjusted for a spatial smooth.

Bug fixes

  • permlmer() (and so permanova.lmer()): when the tested variance is estimated at 0, the likelihood-ratio statistic is 0 up to optimizer noise (e.g. 3e-14). Permuted statistics of 0 then counted as smaller than the observed one, giving a small p-value instead of 1. Statistics are now rounded to 4 decimals before they are compared. In a simulation study (dev/sim-study/) this affected 0.1-0.8% of data sets under the null.

  • predictmeans() and covariatemeans() ignored trans for glm and glmmTMB models with an identity link: a gaussian glmmTMB(log(y) ~ ...) with trans = exp showed no back-transformed means. trans is now used whenever the link is the identity; models with another link still use its inverse.

  • In the back-transformed plots of predictmeans() and covariatemeans(), the data points were not shifted by transOff when the response was transformed before modelling (e.g. a column holding log(y + 1), with transOff = 1), so they sat transOff above the means.

  • R2_glmm():

    • for glmmTMB models with correlated random effects, e.g. (Days | Subject), the random-effect variance was wrong (84.32% instead of the 78.71% that lmer gives for sleepstudy) and the slope was missing from the breakdown. glmmTMB puts correlations on its own scale, so the covariance is now built from VarCorr();
    • the breakdown by term split a correlated term’s columns into two halves instead of by component (lmer too). Each component (intercept, slope) now gets its own share; the covariance between them is only in the random-effect total. Models without correlated terms are unchanged;
    • failed for glmmTMB models with random effects in the zero-inflation part, or with coefficients dropped as aliased;
    • over_disp = TRUE finds the observation-level random effect wherever it is in the formula (glmmTMB keeps the formula’s order).

  • varcomp() for glmer models:

    • the SEs of the variances were wrong: converting from SDs used the derivative 0.5/sqrt(sd) instead of 0.5/sd (0.2845 instead of 0.2280 for the cbpp example; glmmTMB gives 0.2294), and covariances ignored their dependence on the two SDs. vcov_glmerMod(ranpar = "var") now applies the delta method with the full Jacobian;
    • failed for models with more than one variance parameter, e.g. (Days | Subject) (“invalid ‘row.names’ length”).

  • The letterCI help says when CI overlap matches the pairwise tests and when it finds fewer or more differences, with a reference (Maghsoodloo and Huang, 2010; from the 1.1.2 help).

  • Clearer messages for two common mistakes (ideas from James Curran’s isValidTerm() and adj check on the master branch):

    • a modelterm with its factors in another order or letter case: 'Variety:nitro' is not a term of the model. Did you mean 'nitro:Variety'?; otherwise the message lists the model’s terms;
    • a misspelled adj lists the valid choices (before, p.adjust() gave an error that did not mention "tukey"). adj may be given in any letter case, e.g. "Tukey" or "bh", in predictmeans() and contrastmeans(). The contrastmeans() help no longer lists "tukey", which it never supported.

  • residplot():

    • failed for glmmTMB models with coefficients dropped as aliased;
    • in the “random effects vs fitted” panel of glmer and glmmTMB models with a correlated term, e.g. (Days | Subject), the random effects were matched to the wrong columns of Z (ranef() lists them by component, Z by level).

  • ci_mcp() stopped when a lower and upper limit were equal (a mean with SE 0).

  • The internal model.matrix() method for lme models accepts data =.

  • varcomp() for glmmTMB models gave wrong confidence limits (the upper limit could be below the estimate), read correlation parameters as log standard deviations, and had no residual variance. It now gives the same table as for lmer: the variances and covariances of each term (zero-inflation terms prefixed zi.), the residual variance of gaussian models, delta-method SEs (equal to the lmer ones for sleepstudy), and Wald CIs on the log scale for variances and the Fisher z scale for correlations. ci = FALSE now works for these models.

  • semireg_tmb() with predict_info = TRUE: the random-effect covariance was wrong for correlated terms (same cause as in R2_glmm()). A singular covariance is detected without computing all eigenvalues, and a system that is not positive definite falls back to nearPD() instead of failing.

  • contrastmeans() failed with “non-conformable arguments” for every model with a missing treatment combination, even for contrasts that do not involve it. It now works, and stops with a clear message only when a contrast uses a mean that cannot be estimated.

  • Tukey-adjusted p-values within atvar levels used the number of pairs instead of the number of means. With 4 means per level, Tukey was computed for 6 means, so p-values were too large (0.350 instead of 0.197 in the Oats example). For lmer models they also used one averaged df instead of each pair’s df. Both now match emmeans.

  • predictmeans() failed for every lmer model with a missing treatment combination (“replacement has 12 rows, data has 11”).

  • predictmeans() failed for lmer models fitted by ML (REML = FALSE). Satterthwaite df are now used for such fits, with a message; df_term() falls back to Satterthwaite with a warning instead of stopping.

  • permmodels() and CookD() refitted lme/gls models by re-evaluating the model call from inside the package. Data fitted inside a function were not found, and a data set with the same name elsewhere on the search path could be used silently. For example, a local Oats with nitro as a factor was replaced by nlme::Oats, so the permutation tests were for a different model. Refits now use the model’s own data and check that they reproduce its coefficients.

  • Kmatrix(), predictmeans(), permmodels() and CookD() now find the data of gls models fitted inside a function; nlme::getData() does not.

  • CookD() failed for every lmer model: it refitted with ML and then asked for Kenward-Roger df, which needs REML. It now works and agrees with lme.

  • permmodels() failed for gls models without a correlation structure.

  • R2_glmm():

    • for glmmTMB models it now finds data that are not in the global environment;
    • over_disp = TRUE gives a clear message when the model has no observation-level random effect.

  • predictmeans():

    • passing two or more of the deprecated mplot, barplot, pplot, bkplot arguments gave an error instead of a deprecation warning;
    • trans = NULL gave an error.

  • contrastmeans() with permlist counted permuted statistics strictly greater than the observed one. It now counts “greater or equal” (after rounding), as predictmeans() does, so both give the same permutation p-value for the same contrast.

  • predictmeans(), contrastmeans() and permmodels() no longer leave options(scipen = 6) set after they return; printed results look the same.

  • contrastmeans() without ctrmatrix only opens the contrast editor in an interactive session.

  • semipred() failed (“replacement has 0 rows”) on semireg() fits whose data had a numeric variable not in the prediction grid, such as a numeric grouping id in (1 | idnum), because it tried to undo the centring for it in the grid too.

Speed

  • Satterthwaite df (used for lmer models fitted by ML, and by df_term(type = "Satterthwaite")) are computed for all contrasts at once from ingredients computed once per model. They equal lmerTest’s values, about 25x faster for many contrasts (780 pairs: 0.8 s -> 0.03 s), and no longer convert the model to lmerTest’s class.

  • Kenward-Roger computations no longer form or invert the n x n covariance of the data. They use the model’s low-rank structure (Woodbury identity), with the same results as pbkrtest. n = 3,000 takes under 0.05 s instead of 21.5 s; n = 20,000 takes 0.3 s (previously out of reach).

  • Kenward-Roger df are computed for all contrasts at once (identical to pbkrtest::Lb_ddf() row by row), and the adjusted covariance is computed once per predictmeans() call instead of once per model term, for the means, and again for the pairs. predictmeans() on lmer models is about 10-50x faster: Oats split-plot 0.96 s -> 0.09 s; 40 means with 780 pairwise comparisons 5.3 s -> 0.1 s.

  • permmodels() no longer computes Kenward-Roger df for every permutation refit (the df were discarded). About 10x faster for lmer models (99 permutations of the Oats split-plot: 21.8 s -> 2.2 s), with identical permutation p-values.

  • permmodels() and permlmer() use a sparse Cholesky factor and triangular solves instead of a dense n x n inverse.

  • Letter groups (multcompLetters(), used for all letters) are much faster for many means, with identical letters (checked on 375 random cases): 100 means 4.1 s -> 0.3 s; 200 means 103 s -> 2.1 s. The “absorb” step now only checks the letter columns that changed.

  • permmodels() on lmer models takes the t values of each refit from the covariance matrix it already has, instead of calling summary(), which computed it again: about 15-20% faster (300 permutations of the Oats split-plot, type III: 4.3 s -> 3.5 s), with identical results. The nine copies of the per-refit code are now one internal function.

  • R2_glmm() computes its traces without n x n matrices. For n = 4,000 it goes from 4.4 s and 529 MB to 0.01 s with identical results; n = 100,000 now takes 0.02 s.

Non-estimable means

  • Means that cannot be estimated (they depend on aliased coefficients) are now NA in every table, with a message naming them; their pairwise differences are still shown when estimable. Before, a number that depended on the arbitrary choice of aliased coefficient was printed. Means over missing cells keep the 1.x rule (average of the observed cells, with the “Missing treatments’ combination” warning).

Containment df

  • New argument df_method in predictmeans() and contrastmeans() (and type = "containment" in df_term()) for lmer models: "auto" (the default, unchanged: Kenward-Roger for REML fits, Satterthwaite for ML fits), "Kenward-Roger", "Satterthwaite" or "containment". Containment gives the SAS DDFM=CONTAIN df (the smallest rank contribution to [X Z] of the random effects containing the term, else the residual df), with the unadjusted covariance unless vcov_adjust = TRUE is given. For the oats split plot this is 10 for Variety and 45 for Nitro and Variety:Nitro; with a whole plot missing, 9 and 42. The ranks use M’M, so a split plot with n = 6000 and 750 whole plots takes about 3 s.

Bug fixes found by the refactor

  • predictmeans() with both permlist and atvar failed with “undefined columns selected”. It now gives permutation p-values within each atvar level.
  • Factor levels containing ":" (e.g. "Golden:Rain") broke the legacy pairwise tables: atvar failed and the within-factor SEDs and LSDs were computed from misread labels (B4). Level labels are now taken from the label table, never split from row names.
  • A user-supplied Df for an lmer model gave NA p-values for all pairs but the first (“missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” when letters were computed). The given Df is now used for every pair.

Documentation

  • Letter groups, overall and within atvar groups, now come from one function (pm_letter_groups()) that handles unavailable p-values (missing levels or non-estimable differences) the same way everywhere. Fixes repeated errors in the letters with missing p-values, and an error in the mean/SE tables when non-estimable means meet empty cells.

  • Pairwise differences are now checked for estimability, not only the means: with confounded factors (e.g. one volume used only with fine droplets) a difference that depends on a dropped coefficient is NA instead of being computed with that coefficient taken as 0. Letters are given to the means whose comparisons can be estimated, and the message for non-estimable means suggests weights = "cells". Fixes an error (“missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”) in the letters.

  • lmerTest::ranova() on a gaussian semireg() fit failed (“object ‘grp_geo’ not found”), and its refits would have treated the remaining smooth terms as ordinary random intercepts. Gaussian semireg() fits now have class semerLmerTest, whose update() refits through semireg() with the same smooth bases. smoothZ may also be a list given by name.

  • New data set copper (used in the overview article).

  • The deprecated plot arguments (mplot, barplot/bar, pplot, bkplot) turned off every plot not given, so bar = TRUE gave a NULL mean plot. Plots not given now keep their which.plots setting, and the deprecation warning shows the equivalent which.plots call.

  • Fixed (regression in this development version): with nested treatments and one observation per block cell (e.g. treat/contcomp with repl), means were averaged over structurally empty cells and were wrong. Empty cells are now judged on the factors that interact only.

  • atvar with several factors failed (“Names required”) when a group of atvar levels had only one or no observed level of the other factors, or (“replacement has 8 rows, data has 12”) when a group had one level.

  • Within-atvar comparisons: adjusted p-values could be assigned to the wrong group or pair when the groups were not in row order (for example two atvar factors, or empty groups). This came from 1.x. P-values and letters are now matched to groups and levels by name.

  • The examples of permmodels(), permlmer(), permanova.lmer(), semireg(), semireg_tmb() and semipred(), and the lmer example of residplot(), run again (they were commented out). Permutation examples use 99 permutations on one core; slow parts are in \donttest{}, and examples with HRW data run only when HRW is installed. The semireg_tmb() example no longer passes resp_scale, which only semireg() has; the sleepstudy plot uses ggplot2 instead of latticeExtra.

  • For AI assistants and scripted use, inst/llms-context.md describes the result tables (every column of means, pairs and settings), the defaults and common recipes (a test checks that it lists every column). The README, which pkgdown turns into the site’s home page and llms.txt, now describes the package, its main functions and its vignettes.

  • New vignette “Missing cells and non-estimable means”: an empty cell in the oats split plot (the 1.x averaging rule and its warning, comparisons within the observed cells) and confounded factors in a spray trial (NA means with estimable differences, weights = "cells", and writing the nesting into the model).

  • New vignette “Smooth curves in mixed models”: semireg() and semipred() on nlme::Dialyzer, ranova() of the smooth terms, pointwise and simultaneous bands, a difference curve, and predictmeans() on the fit. semipred()’s plot title says when the band is simultaneous.

  • New vignette “Permutation and bootstrap tests”: permmodels() and its use as permlist in predictmeans() and contrastmeans(), permlmer() for a random slope, permanova.lmer(), and bootmodels() for a binomial GLMM, with advice on which to use.

  • New vignette “Link and response scale”: binomial and Poisson GLMs and GLMMs and a log-transformed response (trans = exp), with response-scale means and SEs, odds ratios and ratios, what a back-transformed GLMM mean means, and Piepho’s vs Nakagawa’s R² (R2_model()).

  • New vignette “Contrasts, joint tests and slopes”: the adj methods (including "mvt"), contrast_family() (Dunnett, trends), pm_joint() (slices), pm_slopes() and coef()/vcov() with marginaleffects, on the oats split plot. The getting-started and migrating vignettes link to it.

  • Three vignettes: “Getting started with predictmeans”, “Adjusted R² for generalized linear mixed models” and “Migrating from predictmeans 1.x”.

  • A pkgdown website (built by GitHub Actions and published to GitHub Pages), with two longer worked-example articles: an overview of the package and experimental design and analysis for tree improvement.

  • semireg_tmb() works with glmmTMB >= 1.1.12, which no longer stores Lambdat, Lind and lower (they are rebuilt when missing).

  • R2_glmm() failed for gaussian glmmTMB fits (including semireg_tmb()) with glmmTMB >= 1.1.12, whose dispersion parameter is named betadisp; the fixed effects now come from fixef(model)$cond.

  • New data sets Body_length and Poisson_ind (used in the R² vignette).

Internal

  • The confidence-interval plot uses geom_errorbar(orientation = "y") instead of geom_errorbarh(), which ggplot2 4.0 deprecates; the plot is unchanged.

  • 1:length(x), 1:nrow(x) and 1:ncol(x) are now seq_along(x) / seq_len() throughout (idea from James Curran’s code in 1.1.2); results are unchanged, and empty inputs no longer loop over c(1, 0).

  • Help pages are now written with roxygen2: each page’s source is the block above its function (data sets in R/data.R, the package page in R/predictmeans-package.R), and man/ is generated with roxygen2::roxygenise(roclets = "rd"). NAMESPACE is still maintained by hand. The rendered pages are unchanged.

  • predictmeans() is split into stages (setup, estimate, compare, mean table, back-transform, plots, assemble). All statistics are computed before any plotting, so plot = FALSE skips all graphics work. The work of each stage is done by functions that take their inputs as arguments and return their results, so they can be tested and changed one at a time. Results are unchanged.

Packaging

  • James Curran is credited as a contributor (DESCRIPTION now uses Authors@R).
  • which.plots is documented. DESCRIPTION no longer carries CRAN-generated fields, and NeedsCompilation is “no”.
  • GitHub Actions R CMD check on Linux, macOS and Windows.

Kmatrix() and semipred()

  • Kmatrix() now builds predicted means from a reference grid evaluated with the model’s own basis information. It handles covariates that:
    • enter through transformations: poly(), ns(), bs(), log(), scale(), I();
    • appear only inside interactions (A:x without x, x:z);
    • are mgcv smooth terms (s(), te(), s(x, by = A)). These cases previously stopped with “subscript out of bounds” or “object not found”.
  • Kmatrix() and predictmeans() now support mgcv::gam()/bam() models, using the lpmatrix of the smooths. Random-effect smooths (bs = "re", bs = "fs") are excluded by default (exclude argument).
  • New Kmatrix() argument cov_reduce: fix covariates with any summary function (default mean, e.g. median), or use "average" to average the predictions over the observed covariate values.
  • Kmatrix() now also handles:
    • character and logical predictors;
    • factor(x) terms in the formula (modelterm may be "x" or "factor(x)");
    • models fitted without a data argument;
    • a transformed response together with data =.
  • Kmatrix() returns the reference grid (refgrid) and flags non-estimable rows in attr(K, "estimable").
  • A matrix covariateV for several covariates is now used as a set of joint prediction points, as documented; previously it was ignored.
  • semipred() uses Kmatrix() on the semireg object directly, without refitting an auxiliary lm(). The smooth basis is averaged over the same reference grid as the fixed part. As a result, factors not in modelterm, including by factors of the smooths, are averaged correctly instead of causing an error.
  • The covariate summary printed by prtnum = TRUE now goes through message(), so it can be suppressed.
  • Kmatrix() is faster on large data (about 4-15x on a 20,000-row, 360-cell model).
  • New tests check that results for every case supported by 1.1.1 are unchanged, and compare the new cases with emmeans and mgcv.

Fewer dependencies

  • pbkrtest moved from Imports to Suggests. Kenward-Roger adjusted covariances, df and F tests are computed by a port of pbkrtest’s vcovAdj() and KRmodcomp() that gives the same results in the tests. pbkrtest alone brought 11 tidyverse packages (dplyr, broom, tidyr, …). Installing predictmeans now pulls in 56 packages (112 for 1.1.1).

  • car moved from Imports to Suggests. permmodels() computes its Type II and III tests itself: lm F; glm LR, Wald and F; lme and gls Wald chi-square; lmer Wald chi-square and Kenward-Roger F. They are ported from car and equal car::Anova() in the tests. Installing predictmeans now pulls in 68 packages (112 for 1.1.1).

  • permmodels() with type = "II" now also works for lm models with aliased coefficients. 1.1.1 stopped with an error from car::Anova().

  • plyr is no longer used.

  • HRW, lmeInfo, lmeSplines, plotly and splines2 moved from Imports to Suggests. They are only needed for, respectively:

    • HRW: example data;
    • lmeInfo: varcomp() on lme models;
    • lmeSplines: smZ(type = "smspline");
    • plotly: semipred(threeD = TRUE);
    • splines2: the splines2 spline types in smZ(). A clear message asks for the package when such a feature is used. Installing predictmeans now pulls in 76 packages instead of 112. This also avoids current HRW’s requirement of R >= 4.5.

  • HRW::pointsInPoly() is replaced by an internal copy. It also closes open polygons correctly; HRW’s version adds a spurious vertex when the last vertex does not repeat the first.
